title: Ama and the Lost Little Goat

pages.text: Ama lived in a small village with her family. She had a little goat named Pepe. Pepe had a white spot on his nose.
sentences: Ama lived in a small village with her family.
She had a little goat named Pepe.
Pepe had a white spot on his nose.
pages.alt: A smiling girl with yellow ribbons hugs a small brown goat with a white spot on its nose, in front of a mud-brick house.

pages.text: Every morning Ama gave Pepe fresh water and green leaves. Pepe said, ‘Meh-eh-eh!’ Ama laughed.
sentences: Every morning Ama gave Pepe fresh water and green leaves.
Pepe said, ‘Meh-eh-eh!’ Ama laughed.
pages.alt: Ama holds out green leaves to the goat, who stretches his neck to eat them.

pages.text: One sunny day, Ama went to fetch water. When she came back, Pepe was gone! ‘Pepe! Pepe!’ called Ama.
sentences: One sunny day, Ama went to fetch water.
When she came back, Pepe was gone!
‘Pepe!
Pepe!’ called Ama.
pages.alt: Ama stands holding a bucket, looking at an empty post where the goat was tied. She looks worried.

pages.text: Ama looked by the mango tree. A hen sat there with her chicks. ‘Have you seen Pepe?’ asked Ama. ‘Cluck, cluck, not here,’ said the hen. ‘Try near the well.’
sentences: Ama looked by the mango tree.
A hen sat there with her chicks.
‘Have you seen Pepe?’ asked Ama.
‘Cluck, cluck, not here,’ said the hen.
‘Try near the well.’
pages.alt: Under a mango tree a speckled hen and four chicks talk to Ama.

pages.text: At the well, Ama met old Grandpa Yaw. ‘Have you seen my goat?’ she asked. Grandpa Yaw smiled. ‘I heard a small voice by the big rock.’
sentences: At the well, Ama met old Grandpa Yaw.
‘Have you seen my goat?’ she asked.
Grandpa Yaw smiled.
‘I heard a small voice by the big rock.’
pages.alt: Ama speaks to a smiling elderly man with a white beard beside a village well.

pages.text: Ama ran to the big rock. She stopped and listened. ‘Meh-eh-eh!’ It was Pepe! His rope was caught on a branch.
sentences: Ama ran to the big rock.
She stopped and listened.
‘Meh-eh-eh!’ It was Pepe!
His rope was caught on a branch.
pages.alt: Behind a large rock, the little goat stands with its rope caught on a low branch, and Ama runs toward him.

pages.text: Ama gently freed the rope. Pepe licked her hand. ‘Thank you for helping me,’ Ama told Grandpa Yaw and the hen.
sentences: Ama gently freed the rope.
Pepe licked her hand.
‘Thank you for helping me,’ Ama told Grandpa Yaw and the hen.
pages.alt: Ama unties the rope while the goat nuzzles her hand; the old man and the hen look on, smiling.

pages.text: That evening Ama tied Pepe’s rope to a strong post. ‘Stay close, little one,’ she whispered. Pepe closed his eyes and went to sleep. The end.
sentences: That evening Ama tied Pepe’s rope to a strong post.
‘Stay close, little one,’ she whispered.
Pepe closed his eyes and went to sleep.
The end.
pages.alt: At sunset Ama strokes the sleeping goat beside a sturdy post.

activities.question: Who did Ama lose?
activities.explanation: Ama lost her little goat, Pepe.

activities.prompt: Where do you think Pepe went? Tell a friend your idea.

items: Ama looked by the mango tree.
Ama asked Grandpa Yaw at the well.
Ama found Pepe by the big rock.

activities.prompt: How did Ama feel when Pepe was gone? How did she feel when she found him?

glossary.definition: A small place in the countryside where families live close together.
A deep hole in the ground where people get water.
A thick string used to tie things.
A part of a tree that grows out from the trunk.
